stemMd: What does the passage suggest would happen if the radio-controlled unit were installed exactly as the council intends?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The people of the piazza would arrive at the station earlier than they do now.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The tower would still disagree with the station clock by four minutes.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Nando would be asked to stay on as keeper of the new unit.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The council would need to move the station clock again.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Those who trust the tower would lose the four minutes of margin they have had since 1962.

explanationMd:
This **inference** question asks what follows from facts that are stated separately in the passage.

**What to notice first.** Two facts need joining. Nando explains that the tower was put four minutes ahead "so that anyone who trusted it would arrive early" (1962). Elena says the new unit "will keep perfect time", with no such offset unless someone adds it.

**The step that settles it.** An accurate tower shows the true time. Anyone who has relied on the tower to catch the 8.10 has had four minutes in hand; with an exact clock those four minutes disappear. The passage does not state this, but both facts force it.

**Testing the others.** People who trust the tower would arrive later than they do now, not earlier. The new unit would show the true time, so the four-minute gap would close rather than remain. And the passage says nothing about Nando remaining as keeper or about the station clock being moved again.

**How to check.** Ask yourself what the offset was for, then what happens when it is gone. Elena's closing note to the installer ("Set the tower four minutes ahead") shows that she has drawn the same conclusion.

distractorRationale.a: The reverse follows. The tower now runs four minutes fast, so those who trust it arrive early; an accurate tower removes that head start.
distractorRationale.b: The new unit is described as accurate to a second a year, so it would agree with the correct time; the four-minute difference is what is being removed.
distractorRationale.c: The passage says only that the new unit will replace the old mechanism, which Elena has been sent to learn; it says nothing about who will look after the new unit, and nothing suggests that Nando stays on.
distractorRationale.d: Nothing in the passage connects the new unit with any change to the station clock, which is a different clock.

accessibilityText: A question about the accompanying short narrative about a tower clock. It asks what the passage suggests would happen if the radio-controlled unit were installed exactly as the council intends. Five possible outcomes are offered.

provenance.notes: Original item written against the original passage polito-til-a-passage-tower-clock-302, authored alongside it. Every distractor rests on a named misreading of that passage.

review.author: polito-til-a-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The council calls the four-minute lead a fault and intends a unit that keeps perfect time. Installed that way, the tower would show true time, and those who trust it would lose the lead that was set in 1962 so they would arrive early. B is the opposite of accurate installation. A reverses the effect. C and D have no support. Elena's note changes the plan, but the stem rules it out with 'exactly as the council intends'. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: The council calls the four-minute lead a fault and wants a unit that keeps perfect time, so installing it as the council intends would remove the lead that has been there since 1962. B describes what would happen under Elena's installer note, not under the council's intention, and the stem's 'exactly as the council intends' rules it out. A is the reverse (people would arrive later, not earlier), and C and D are not supported.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: the tower was put ahead so trusting townspeople would arrive early and the new unit would keep exact time, so the extra four minutes would be lost; the other choices reverse the effect or introduce events the passage does not mention. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication.
